blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how businesses keep track of all their transactions? The answer lies in the ledger accounts.

blocks.markdown: In accounting, a ledger is a book or computer file used to record and total economic transactions measured in terms of a monetary unit of account by account type, with debits and credits in separate columns and a beginning monetary balance and ending monetary balance for each account.

blocks.title: Definition of Ledger Accounts
blocks.text: A ledger account is a record of all transactions affecting a particular item, such as cash, accounts receivable, or accounts payable.

blocks.markdown: Ledger accounts are classified into three types: personal, real, and nominal accounts. Personal accounts relate to individuals or organizations, real accounts relate to assets, and nominal accounts relate to income, expenses, gains, and losses.

blocks.title: Posting to a T-account
blocks.prompt: Let's post a transaction of N10,000 cash received from Chinedu into the ledger.

steps.text: Identify the accounts affected: Cash (real account) and Chinedu (personal account).
Debit the Cash account because cash is increasing.
Credit Chinedu's account because his liability to the business is decreasing.

blocks.answer: Cash account is debited with N10,000, and Chinedu's account is credited with N10,000.

blocks.markdown: Balancing a ledger account involves ensuring that the total debits equal the total credits. If not, the difference is carried down to the next period.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always remember the rule: Debit the receiver, credit the giver for personal accounts; Debit what comes in, credit what goes out for real accounts; Debit expenses and losses, credit income and gains for nominal accounts.

points: Ledger accounts are crucial for recording all financial transactions.
They are classified into personal, real, and nominal accounts.
Balancing ledger accounts is essential to ensure accuracy in financial reporting.
